title: Sperm donors need limits, says a European fertility group

paragraphs.text: Ties van der Meer doesn’t know how many siblings he has.
paragraphs.translation: Ties van der Meer 不知道他有多少個兄弟姐妹。

paragraphs.text: The 47-year-old was conceived at a private fertility clinic in the Netherlands using sperm provided by an anonymous donor. After the Netherlands banned anonymous donation in 2004, the doctor who ran the clinic destroyed records that might have identified those donors, he says.
paragraphs.translation: 這位 47 歲的男子是在荷蘭一家私人不孕症診所，使用匿名捐贈者提供的精子受孕的。他說，在荷蘭於 2004 年禁止匿名捐贈後，經營該診所的醫生銷毀了可能識別這些捐贈者身分的記錄。

paragraphs.text: He describes the situation as “problematic.” Children have a right to know their biological parents, he says. While he did ultimately track down one sibling, who helped him identify his father along with other genetic relatives, he may have others he’ll never find.
paragraphs.translation: 他形容這種情況「有問題」。他說，孩子有權知道自己的親生父母。雖然他最終追蹤到了一位兄弟姐妹，並幫助他與其他遺傳親屬一起確認了他的父親，但他可能還有其他永遠找不到的親人。

paragraphs.text: Other donor-conceived people who have been able to track down siblings have found they have tens or even hundreds of them. One donor-conceived woman who found 25 half-siblings over the course of seven years told the Guardian, “It does make you feel a bit mass-produced.”
paragraphs.translation: 其他能夠追蹤到兄弟姐妹的受贈受孕者發現，他們有數十個甚至數百個兄弟姐妹。一位在七年時間裡找到了 25 個同父異母兄弟姐妹的受贈受孕女性告訴《衛報》：「這確實讓你覺得自己有點像批量生產的產品。」

paragraphs.text: We need international limits on the number of children a single donor can contribute to, a European fertility organization argued yesterday. At a conference in London, members laid out plans to start with a Europe-wide limit.
paragraphs.translation: 一個歐洲生育組織昨天辯稱，我們需要對單個捐贈者可以貢獻的孩子數量設定國際限制。在倫敦舉行的一場會議上，成員們提出了從全歐洲範圍的限制開始的計劃。

paragraphs.text: Today many countries, including the UK, have banned anonymous egg and sperm donation. But anonymity can’t be guaranteed even in places where it is technically allowed. Genetic tests offered by companies like Ancestry and 23andMe, along with genetic registries, have made it much easier for donor-conceived people to find parents and siblings who share their genes.
paragraphs.translation: 今天，包括英國在內的許多國家已經禁止匿名卵子和精子捐贈。但即使在技術上允許匿名的地方，匿名也無法得到保證。Ancestry 和 23andMe 等公司提供的基因檢測，以及基因登記庫，使得受贈受孕者更容易找到與他們基因相同的父母和兄弟姐妹。

paragraphs.text: And because sperm can be frozen and stored for years before it is eventually used, the current set-up can result in situations where donor-conceived people discover the identity of a genetic parent only after the person’s death. They might also find that they have siblings of very different ages, all around the world.
paragraphs.translation: 由於精子在最終使用前可以冷凍保存多年，目前的設置可能會導致受贈受孕者僅在遺傳父母去世後才發現其身分。他們還可能發現自己在世界各地有著年齡跨度很大的兄弟姐妹。

paragraphs.text: Some people are finding hundreds of siblings. Sperm from Jonathan Meijer, a Dutch man who began donating in 2007, was used to conceive between 550 and 600 children. (Stichting Donorkind, a foundation and advocacy group for donor-conceived people that’s chaired by van der Meer, took him to court, and he was ordered to stop donating in 2023.)
paragraphs.translation: 有些人發現了數百名兄弟姐妹。2007 年開始捐贈的荷蘭男子 Jonathan Meijer 的精子被用於孕育了 550 到 600 名孩子。（Stichting Donorkind 是一個由 van der Meer 擔任主席的受贈受孕者基金會和倡導團體，該團體將他告上法庭，他於 2023 年被勒令停止捐贈。）

paragraphs.text: Stories like these can be distressing for donor-conceived people. And there are other reasons why limits are considered important. The offspring of a prolific donor might be at risk of unknowingly forming romantic or sexual relationships, for instance. And some people are concerned that a donor with a harmful genetic mutation might pass that down to many children.
paragraphs.translation: 這樣的故事對於受贈受孕者來說可能令人感到痛苦。此外，限制被認為很重要的還有其他原因。例如，多產捐贈者的後代可能面臨在不知情的情況下建立浪漫或性關係的風險。一些人擔心患有有害基因突變的捐贈者可能會將其遺傳給許多孩子。

paragraphs.text: This is unlikely, given the level of screening that most donors undergo. But it has happened. A man who donated his sperm to a sperm bank in Denmark was found to have a genetic mutation that significantly increased the risk of multiple cancers. But his sperm had already been used to conceive at least 197 children across Europe. Some of those children developed cancer. Some died.
paragraphs.translation: 考慮到大多數捐贈者接受的篩查水平，這種情況不太可能發生。但它確實發生過。一名向丹麥精子庫捐贈精子的男子被發現患有一種基因突變，會顯著增加患多種癌症的風險。但他的精子已經被用於在歐洲各地孕育了至少 197 名孩子。其中一些孩子患上了癌症，有些人已經去世。

paragraphs.text: Many countries already have legal limits for donors. In Malta and Cyprus, for example, both egg and sperm donors are allowed to contribute to the birth of just a single child, according to data presented at the European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology (ESHRE) meeting in London on July 8.
paragraphs.translation: 根據 7 月 8 日在倫敦舉行的歐洲人類生殖與胚胎學學會 (ESHRE) 會議上公佈的數據，許多國家已經對捐贈者設定了法律限制。例如，在馬爾他與塞浦路斯，卵子和精子捐贈者都只被允許為一個孩子的出生做出貢獻。

paragraphs.text: Other countries set limits based on the number of families a single donor can contribute to, allowing recipients to have children who share a genetic link. In the UK, that limit is set at 10 families per donor.
paragraphs.translation: 其他國家根據單個捐贈者可以貢獻的家庭數量來設定限制，允許受贈者擁有具有遺傳聯繫的孩子。在英國，該限制設定為每位捐贈者 10 個家庭。

paragraphs.text: But these limits are difficult to enforce, partly because donated gametes don’t necessarily stay in their original country. In Denmark, the national limit is set at 12 families. But the country is a major exporter of sperm. In the UK, for example, more than half of sperm donations in 2020 were imported—with most of those coming from either Denmark or the US.
paragraphs.translation: 但這些限制很難執行，部分原因是捐贈的配子不一定留在原產國。在丹麥，國家限制設定為 12 個家庭。但該國是主要的精子出口國。例如，在英國，2020 年超過一半的精子捐贈是進口的，其中大部分來自丹麥或美國。

paragraphs.text: “The only thing that really makes sense is a transnational limit,” Jackson Kirkman-Brown, a professor of reproductive biology at the University of Birmingham, said at the meeting.
paragraphs.translation: 伯明翰大學生殖生物學教授 Jackson Kirkman-Brown 在會議上表示：「唯一真正有意義的是跨國限制。」

paragraphs.text: Kirkman-Brown and his colleagues have spent months putting together a document that represents ESHRE’s position on these limits. After consulting with fertility specialists, clinics, sperm and egg banks, donors, and donor-conceived people, the team has developed a plan to start with a Europe-wide limit on sperm and egg donations.
paragraphs.translation: Kirkman-Brown 和他的同事花了幾個月的時間編寫了一份文件，代表了 ESHRE 對這些限制的立場。在諮詢了生育專家、診所、精子和卵子庫、捐贈者以及受贈受孕者後，該團隊制定了一項計劃，從對精子和卵子捐贈設定全歐洲範圍的限制開始。

paragraphs.text: ESHRE is calling on sperm and egg banks, as well as fertility clinics, to respect an initial limit of 50 families per donor. That’s still very high, according to a handful of people I spoke to at the meeting. But at least it’s a start.
paragraphs.translation: ESHRE 呼籲精子和卵子庫以及生育診所遵守每位捐贈者 50 個家庭的初步限制。據我在會議上交談過的少數幾個人說，這個數字仍然非常高。但至少這是一個開始。

paragraphs.text: Europe should move toward setting limits at 15 families per donor, Kirkman-Brown said. “We may find that 15 is also too high,” says Vasanti Jadva, who studies the psychological well-being of people conceived using donated eggs, sperm, and embryos at City St George’s in London. “We still don’t know what the right number is.”
paragraphs.translation: Kirkman-Brown 表示，歐洲應該朝著將限制設定為每位捐贈者 15 個家庭的方向邁進。「我們可能會發現 15 個也太高了，」在倫敦聖喬治大學研究受贈受孕者心理健康的 Vasanti Jadva 說。「我們仍然不知道正確的數字是多少。」

paragraphs.text: It will be difficult to enforce these limits, too. And if they end up limiting the supply of donor sperm, there’s a chance that some people will turn to unregulated sperm donations from people who do not undergo health screening. Unregulated donations can lead to other problems for prospective parents, including the possibility that donors will seek parental rights over the children conceived using their sperm.
paragraphs.translation: 執行這些限制也將會很困難。如果它們最終限制了捐贈精子的供應，那麼有些人可能會轉向來自不接受健康篩查的人的非正規精子捐贈。非正規捐贈可能會給未來的父母帶來其他問題，包括捐贈者可能會對使用其精子孕育的孩子尋求父母權利的可能性。

paragraphs.text: And it will be even harder to establish international limits. When I asked the American Society of Reproductive Medicine for its thoughts on ESHRE’s proposed limits, a representative directed me to a guidance document saying “it has been suggested” that for a population of 800,000, single donors should be limited to “no more than 25 births” in order to avoid the risk that relatives will have children together. (Considering the US has a population of over 340 million, the total figure could be pretty high, but many sperm banks opt to limit the number of families contributed to by a single donor at around 25.)
paragraphs.translation: 建立國際限制將會更加困難。當我詢問美國生殖醫學學會對 ESHRE 提議的限制的看法時，一位代表指引我參考一份指導文件，其中提到「有人建議」，在 80 萬人口中，單個捐贈者應限制在「不超過 25 次分娩」，以避免親屬共同生育子女的風險。（考慮到美國人口超過 3.4 億，總數可能會相當高，但許多精子庫選擇將單個捐贈者貢獻的家庭數量限制在 25 個左右。）

paragraphs.text: Van der Meer thinks that even a limit of five families from a single donor would be high. International donation makes it even harder for donor-conceived people to connect with genetic relatives, so the limit for international contributions should be set at two families, he says.
paragraphs.translation: Van der Meer 認為，即使是單個捐贈者五個家庭的限制也算高。他說，國際捐贈使得受贈受孕者更難與遺傳親屬聯繫，因此國際貢獻的限制應設定為兩個家庭。

paragraphs.text: Still, he thinks ESHRE’s suggested limit is a “positive first step.” Van der Meer has managed to track down a sibling, his father, and nephews, aunts, and uncles. He hopes that future policies respect the rights of donor-conceived children to know, and be in contact with, their genetic relatives.
paragraphs.translation: 儘管如此，他認為 ESHRE 建議的限制是「積極的第一步」。Van der Meer 已經成功追蹤到了一個兄弟姐妹、他的父親，以及侄子、阿姨和叔叔。他希望未來的政策能尊重受贈受孕孩子了解並聯繫其遺傳親屬的權利。

paragraphs.text: “But,” he says, “you have to start somewhere.”
paragraphs.translation: 「但是，」他說，「你總得從某個地方開始。」

paragraphs.text: The country wants to become a global leader in brain implants. Strong government support is expected to help accelerate that process.

paragraphs.text: Researchers are decoding how signals move between body and brain, with implications for how we understand and treat conditions from obesity to anxiety.
paragraphs.translation: 研究人員正在解碼信號如何在身體和大腦之間移動，這對我們理解和治療從肥胖到焦慮的各種疾病都有影響。

paragraphs.text: The “steroid olympics” were a circus—and a window into our culture
paragraphs.translation: 「類固醇奧運會」是一場鬧劇——也是窺探我們文化的一扇窗

paragraphs.text: Dozens of athletes on performance-enhancing drugs competed in the Enhanced Games. Organizers hope it'll sell a lot of peptides and other supplements.
paragraphs.translation: 數十名使用體能增強藥物的運動員參加了「增強運動會」。主辦方希望這能帶動胜肽和其他補充劑的銷量。

paragraphs.translation: 追求青春的下一步是一種稱為「化學重編程」的技術。
